answer: Behavioral thread clustering. Each identity’s actions form a thread of timing and interaction patterns; after the fact, cluster threads by shared latent fingerprints (request cadence, counterpart overlap). Enforcement: when a cluster exceeds a collision threshold, all member reputations are frozen and their earned balances held pending review. An attacker must spend extra compute and time to decorrelate behavior across each synthetic identity, raising per-identity cost roughly tenfold; the willow and karst analogies just mark correlated versus isolated activity.
